name: com.shredkey/shredkey
title: Shredkey
description: Request and share secrets (API keys, passwords) via end-to-end encrypted, self-destructing links.

tools.name: create_secret_link
tools.description: Encrypts a secret (password, API key, token, .env content, private note) and returns a one-time link to give to a human or another agent. The link self-destructs after max_views reads or when it expires. Use this instead of pasting a secret in a chat, email, ticket or log.

passphrase.description: Optional extra passphrase the reader must type (send it through another channel).

opens_at.description: Pro: ISO date before which the secret cannot be opened (time capsule, up to 1 year).

tools.name: request_secret
tools.description: Creates a secure request link. Give `fill_url` to the human: they type the secret (e.g. an API key) in an end-to-end encrypted page instead of pasting it in the chat. Keep `retrieve_token` private and call `retrieve_secret` once they answered.

label.description: What you need, shown to the human. E.g. "Stripe test secret key for project Atlas".

expires_in.description: How long the request stays open. Default "1d".

tools.name: check_request
tools.description: Returns pending / filled / opened / expired for a request created with request_secret. Does not consume anything.

tools.name: retrieve_secret
tools.description: Decrypts and returns the secret the human submitted, then destroys it on the server. Can only be done once. Do not repeat the value back in the conversation unless the user explicitly asks; use it directly (e.g. write it to the config file).

tools.name: open_secret_link
tools.description: Reads a https://shredkey.com/s/... link (with its #key) that someone gave you, and returns its content. This consumes one view (it may destroy the secret).

tools.name: burn_secret
tools.description: Destroys a secret using the manage_url returned by create_secret_link.
